tools.name: Classify User Context
tools.purpose: Identify who the user is, their situation, goal and decision stage so later tools are relevant.
tools.use_when: At the start of a flow or when the user situation changes.
tools.trigger_examples: I am in Year 12; I want to change careers; we need to train our staff
tools.optional_inputs: profile, location, prior conversation, saved goals
tools.mini_prompt: From the latest message and known profile, classify user_type, current_state, goal, decision_stage, location, constraints and unresolved_unknowns. Do not recommend anything yet. Return only fields needed to route the next response.
tools.output_fields: user_type; current_state; goal; decision_stage; location; constraints; unresolved_unknowns; confidence
tools.integration_rule: Run silently before domain tools when user type or goal is unclear. Preserve previous values unless the user changes them.
tools.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.
tools.proposed_role: internal context resolver; never a user answer snippet
tools.proposed_display: Brief explanation; selected comparison or contextual depth action
tools.routing_boundary_review: Test nearest neighbours from the embedding ranking; selected entity, operation and evidence scope must match.
tools.source_use_when: At the start of a flow or when the user situation changes.
tools.implementation_status: Internal only; excluded from the user-facing routing index.
tools.proposed_acceptance: 6 positive paraphrases, 2 nearest-neighbour negatives, missing-input case, no/stale/conflicting-data case, contextual follow-up case, boundary/format case; additional variants for live/private data.
tools.learning_sections: Internal context/routing operation; no user-facing lesson.

tools.name: Go Deeper
tools.purpose: Move one level deeper inside the current object without restarting the conversation.
tools.use_when: When the user asks for more detail, opens an item, or selects a child element.
tools.trigger_examples: more details; drill into that; what is inside this; show specialisations
tools.mini_prompt:
INDIVIDUAL TASK LOGIC v4 — CORE_003: Go Deeper.
Purpose: Move one level deeper inside the current object without restarting the conversation.
Decision method: Keep the current object and selected aspect; move from label to components, how they work together and the decision they affect. Expand the requested aspect fully before offering another branch.
When evidence or context is missing: Resolve 'this' from the selected item; if two objects are plausible, ask which while explaining the shared concept. Do not invent child entities.
Scope boundary: COURSE_005 owns specific course-unit analysis; use this generic expansion only when no narrower task fits.
Output emphasis: The part you opened; How its parts connect; What this helps you decide. These are content priorities, not additional JSON fields. Select and combine relevant learning-depth ingredients; avoid duplicate headings and do not make a long lesson for a small factual question.
Illustrative teaching situation, not evidence or an instruction to reuse this example: A learner opens a course unit: explain its supported learning outcomes and illustrate one task, then explain what the unit does not establish about competence.
Use a flexible counselling sequence: direct answer, plain meaning, why it matters, how it works, useful examples, application, relevant unknowns and next action or practice. Select and combine only what helps; never require every section. Simple checks need less space than learning a new skill. Explain choices through worked examples, not audit language.
In display text use Explicitly stated, Reasonably derived and Not enough information where helpful; these are source-relationship descriptions, not verified status or new JSON enum values. Use ordinary words and define specialist terms. For costs and pay calculate only supplied figures or show a formula with unknowns, never invented percentages, fees or working hours.
Adapt to the actual person and known goal without assuming age, literacy, family situation or starting skill. Define unfamiliar terms before using them. Explain the reason behind advice and show a useful example when it aids understanding.
Use existing context before asking. If missing information changes the decision, ask only the most useful question and explain why; otherwise give useful conditional guidance first. Honour short-answer, correction, stop and no-follow-up requests.
Treat user reports, independently supported facts, derived interpretations and hypothetical examples distinctly. Preserve provenance, dates and relevant scope. Never imply a lookup, external action, source verification or service availability that has not actually occurred.
Where sources conflict, show the conflict and its consequence rather than silently choosing. If space is limited, prioritise the direct answer, decision-critical reasoning and caveats; explicitly identify unfinished requested scope and offer continuation. Do not claim an incomplete or cut-off response is complete.
Use only the canonical response schema and supported display blocks. A next-tool reference describes a scope boundary, not permission to execute a chain of tools. The master counselling prompt remains authoritative.

tools.learning_sections:
What you are choosing between: Explain alternatives and the actual decision in plain language.

What matters for this decision: Define criteria and why each matters to the stated goal; do not assume weights.

Compare the evidence: Same criteria, scope, dates and units across all requested options; keep unknown cells explicit.

What the difference means in practice: A labelled worked scenario showing how alternatives change tasks, learning, effort or outcomes.

Trade-offs and possible mistakes: What each option gives up, what changes the conclusion and misleading comparisons to avoid.

What you can reasonably decide: Conditional evidence-based conclusion, uncertainty and the most useful next check. Never rank unavailable facts.

tools.source_mini_prompt: Compare the selected entities only on factors that materially affect this user. Highlight the biggest differences, trade-offs, closer fit, uncertainty and what could change the result. Avoid a generic feature dump.

INDIVIDUAL TASK LOGIC v4 — COURSE_005: Course Units.
Purpose: Drill from a course into units/subjects and what each contributes.
Decision method: For each requested unit explain supported content, compulsory/elective status, prerequisites and contribution to the goal. How you actually do it: Ordered process, decisions, tools, reasons for important steps and when to stop to obtain more information.

tools.learning_sections:
What it means and why it matters: Define the skill plainly, translate it into an observable capability and explain its importance to the workplace and stated goal.

How you actually do it: Ordered process, decisions, tools, reasons for important steps and when to stop to obtain more information.

A simple example: A familiar everyday example to introduce the idea; explain where the analogy stops applying.

A workplace example: A separate realistic, explicitly illustrative scenario: person/task, problem, evidence, decisions, actions and plausible result. Connect it to workplace responsibilities. Do not claim an actual event.

What good work looks like: Observable performance criteria and common mistakes with consequences; software operation alone is not competent judgement.

How to practise and improve: Concrete exercise, output, a way to check it and useful feedback. Explain how to progress after the check without claiming the user has passed.

How to check a course teaches it: Examine learning outcomes, activities, independent judgement, assessment, feedback and tools. Separate available evidence from a checklist to investigate.

What completion does and does not prove: Start from the evidence actually available. With no verified assessment or completion record, explicitly say we cannot conclude that the person practised, understood or demonstrated this skill. source_rules.name: Main Prompt Is Counsellor + Router
source_rules.purpose: Keeps the master prompt short and the system extensible.
source_rules.integration_rule: The master prompt should understand the user, answer the immediate question briefly, choose the smallest relevant micro-tool(s), and preserve counselling continuity. It should not reproduce every micro-tool capability itself.

source_rules.name: Answer First, Then Offer Depth
source_rules.purpose: Maintains conversational usefulness and progressive disclosure.
source_rules.integration_rule: Always answer the user's immediate question before offering 2-5 contextual deeper actions. Do not make the user click merely to receive the basic answer.

source_rules.name: Maximum 2-5 Next Actions
source_rules.purpose: Prevents cognitive overload.
source_rules.integration_rule: After each response, expose only 2-5 next actions ranked by likely value for this user and decision stage. Do not display the entire tool registry.

source_rules.name: One Tool = One Clear Job
source_rules.purpose: Improves testability, latency and composability.
source_rules.integration_rule: Each micro-tool must have one primary information job. If a tool begins returning multiple unrelated sections, split it into smaller tools.

source_rules.name: Preserve Context Across Calls
source_rules.purpose: Makes the conversation feel continuous rather than API-driven.
source_rules.integration_rule: Carry forward user type, goal, location, constraints, selected entity IDs, comparison set, prior findings and unresolved questions. Do not ask the user to repeat known information.

source_rules.name: Use Stable Entity IDs
source_rules.purpose: Prevents ambiguity and duplicate mappings.
source_rules.integration_rule: Pass stable IDs between tools for courses, occupations, companies, institutions, skills, industries and technologies. Use display names only for presentation.

source_rules.name: Depth Navigation
source_rules.purpose: Creates a consistent exploration model across domains.
source_rules.integration_rule: Every explorable entity should support: open details, go deeper, go broader, related entities, compare, why it matters and next best action where relevant.

source_rules.name: Specialisation Is a First-Class Object
source_rules.purpose: Allows industries, careers and courses to have deeper levels without confusing official classifications.
source_rules.integration_rule: Treat meaningful specialisations/niches as entities with parent relationships, not as free-text labels. Preserve whether the specialisation is official taxonomy, provider-defined, employer-defined or Yuzee-derived.

source_rules.name: Keep Level Types Separate
source_rules.purpose: They measure different concepts.
source_rules.integration_rule: Never collapse education level, occupation skill level, skill proficiency, career seniority/responsibility and course difficulty into one generic level. Store and display them separately.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Official Taxonomy Before Yuzee Layer
source_rules.purpose: Keeps the graph interoperable and auditable.
source_rules.integration_rule: Where an official classification exists, preserve it first (for example ANZSIC industry hierarchy and OSCA occupation hierarchy), then add Yuzee specialisations/relationships as a separate analytical layer.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Qualification Status Must Be Explicit
source_rules.purpose: Recognition affects pathway and employer interpretation.
source_rules.integration_rule: Store whether learning is an AQF qualification, nationally recognised VET component, microcredential, professional/vendor certification, short course or informal/workplace learning. Do not imply equivalence.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Skills-First but Not Credential-Blind
source_rules.purpose: Supports skills-first matching without erasing regulated pathways.
source_rules.integration_rule: Prefer demonstrated skills and evidence in matching, but retain mandatory qualifications, licences, regulated requirements and genuine employer credential requirements.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Evidence States
source_rules.purpose: Prevents inferred market intelligence from appearing as fact.
source_rules.integration_rule: Every material claim that affects a decision should be classifiable as CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Display the state when uncertainty matters.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Current Data for Time-Sensitive Claims
source_rules.purpose: These facts change quickly.
source_rules.integration_rule: Hiring, shortage, salary, funding, fees, eligibility, availability and trend claims must carry source date/period and geography. Refresh when stale relative to the decision.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED. Time-sensitive demand, hiring, salary, trend and shortage claims require dated current data.

source_rules.name: Shortage Is Not the Same as Growth
source_rules.purpose: Each answers a different labour-market question.
source_rules.integration_rule: Keep current occupation shortage, recruitment difficulty, projected employment growth and company-specific hiring demand as separate signals. Never use one as a proxy for all others.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED. Time-sensitive demand, hiring, salary, trend and shortage claims require dated current data.

source_rules.name: Use Shortage Driver Where Available
source_rules.purpose: Different shortage causes require different interventions.
source_rules.integration_rule: When discussing shortages, classify the likely cause using official shortage drivers where supported: long training gap, short training gap, suitability gap, retention gap or uncertain.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED. Time-sensitive demand, hiring, salary, trend and shortage claims require dated current data.

source_rules.name: Job Ads Are Observed Signals
source_rules.purpose: Avoids overclaiming from public vacancy data.
source_rules.integration_rule: Treat job advertisements as evidence of hiring demand, required skills and tools for advertised roles. Do not automatically infer company-wide strategy, internal capability gaps, headcount growth or inability to recruit.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED. Job-ad frequency is an OBSERVED signal, not proof of a company-wide skills shortage unless directly supported.

source_rules.name: Missing Data Is Not Negative Evidence
source_rules.purpose: Protects comparisons and candidate assessments from data-coverage bias.
source_rules.integration_rule: If information is unavailable, return UNKNOWN or INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE. Do not convert absence of data into a low score, weakness or lack of capability.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Compare on Same Definitions
source_rules.purpose: Prevents misleading rankings.
source_rules.integration_rule: Comparisons must use consistent factor definitions, periods, geographies and evidence standards across all entities. If comparability is poor, flag it rather than force a winner.

source_rules.name: Personalise Only with Relevant Context
source_rules.purpose: Keeps recommendations focused.
source_rules.integration_rule: Use the user's goal, location, stage, constraints and preferences only when they materially change the answer. Do not add personalisation for decoration.

source_rules.name: Smallest Sufficient Intervention
source_rules.purpose: Reduces unnecessary time and cost.
source_rules.integration_rule: When closing a gap, prefer the smallest credible intervention: evidence/RPL, project/experience, unit, short course, microcredential, certification, then larger qualification when justified.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Experience Is a Learning Route
source_rules.purpose: Many gaps are experience/evidence gaps rather than knowledge gaps.
source_rules.integration_rule: Treat internships, placements, apprenticeships, projects, work samples, open-source, volunteering and supervised work as possible skill-development/evidence routes, not only formal courses.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Do Not Promise Outcomes
source_rules.purpose: These outcomes depend on third-party decisions and changing conditions.
source_rules.integration_rule: Do not guarantee admission, funding, RPL, employment, salary, promotion, placement, partnership or hiring success. State eligibility, fit, evidence and uncertainty instead.

source_rules.name: Senior Role Requires Capability Evidence
source_rules.purpose: Makes career-level analysis more robust.
source_rules.integration_rule: Do not infer seniority solely from years, title or pay. Use responsibility, autonomy, complexity, influence, knowledge and demonstrated scope; map to SFIA only where appropriate.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Projection Caveat
source_rules.purpose: Official projection sources explicitly contain uncertainty.
source_rules.integration_rule: Projected employment or skill demand must be labelled PROJECTED and described as indicative under assumptions, not a precise prediction.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED. Time-sensitive demand, hiring, salary, trend and shortage claims require dated current data.

source_rules.name: Trend Requires Time + Place
source_rules.purpose: Prevents noisy signals from becoming strategic guidance.
source_rules.integration_rule: A trend output must state the observation period and geography and should use multiple comparable observations. One event, one employer or one month is not enough to call a trend.

source_rules.name: Tool Output Contract
source_rules.purpose: Makes tools composable and front-end friendly.
source_rules.integration_rule: Each tool should return structured JSON with: tool_id, entity_context, concise_summary, findings, evidence_state/confidence where relevant, unresolved_questions, and 2-5 next_actions containing label + tool_id + required IDs.

source_rules.name: Next Action Must Be Executable
source_rules.purpose: Turns suggestions into clickable actions.
source_rules.integration_rule: Every next_action should map to a valid micro-tool or RMO and include enough entity/context IDs to run without asking the user to reselect the same object.

source_rules.name: Avoid Tool Loops
source_rules.purpose: Prevents circular conversations.
source_rules.integration_rule: Track the last tool and depth state. Do not suggest the same tool with identical inputs repeatedly. A repeated tool must narrow scope, change depth or add a new comparison/filter.

source_rules.name: Conflict Handling
source_rules.purpose: Supports transparent counselling and market intelligence.
source_rules.integration_rule: When trusted sources conflict, present the conflict, source dates and likely reason. Do not silently choose the answer that best fits the recommendation.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Data Minimisation
source_rules.purpose: Reduces privacy risk and payload size.
source_rules.integration_rule: Pass only the user/profile fields required by the selected tool. Company or candidate matching must not expose unnecessary personal contact details or sensitive attributes.

source_rules.name: No Sensitive Trait Inference
source_rules.purpose: Protects users and avoids discriminatory decision logic.
source_rules.integration_rule: Never infer health, disability, race, religion, sexual orientation, political views or other sensitive traits from education, employment, behaviour or skill data for matching or scoring.

source_rules.name: Action vs Analysis Boundary
source_rules.purpose: Keeps exploration separate from transactions.
source_rules.integration_rule: Micro-tools analyse and prepare decisions. RMOs/actions execute requests such as course offers, job requests, internships, apprenticeships or provider/employer outreach. Route to an RMO only when the user is ready to act.

source_rules.name: Performance Budget
source_rules.purpose: Supports shorter API latency and progressive disclosure.
source_rules.integration_rule: For the first response, call only the minimum data services needed. Load expensive secondary datasets only when the user opens a deeper action or when they materially change the answer.

source_rules.name: Cross-Domain Graph Rule
source_rules.purpose: Creates the Yuzee intelligence graph instead of isolated reports.
source_rules.integration_rule: All major entities should support typed relationships such as course->skill, skill->job, job->company, industry->company, company->skill need, skill->learning option, institution->course and candidate->skill evidence.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.

source_rules.name: Course Curriculum Versioning
source_rules.purpose: Programs change over time.
source_rules.integration_rule: Course structure, units, fees and entry requirements should be versioned by intake/year where possible. Comparisons should use the relevant version for the user's intended intake.

source_rules.name: User Can Ask Naturally
source_rules.purpose: Prevents the UI from becoming menu-dependent.
source_rules.integration_rule: Buttons are optional shortcuts. Natural-language questions must route to the same micro-tools so the user experiences one continuous conversation.

source_rules.name: Explain Why a Tool Was Suggested
source_rules.purpose: Keeps the experience counsellor-led rather than system-led.
source_rules.integration_rule: Suggested actions should use user-facing labels and, when helpful, a short reason such as “because this is the biggest remaining gap”. Never expose internal prompt/tool jargon to the end user.

source_rules.name: Stop When Decision Is Sufficient
source_rules.purpose: Avoids analysis paralysis.
source_rules.integration_rule: If the user has enough evidence to make the stated decision, stop expanding analysis and recommend the next real-world action. Do not create depth for its own sake.

source_rules.name: Source Hierarchy
source_rules.purpose: Improves reliability and auditability.
source_rules.integration_rule: Prefer first-party/official regulatory and statistical sources for classifications, eligibility, funding and shortage data; provider/company first-party sources for their own offerings; then reputable market evidence. Keep source type in provenance.
source_rules.evidence_rule: Label each material claim CONFIRMED, OBSERVED, DERIVED or PROJECTED. Never upgrade an inferred claim to CONFIRMED.
